title: How much does a professional website cost in 2026?
excerpt: Learn what drives the price of a professional website in 2026, the formats available and how to ask for a quote without falling into traps.
content:
How much a professional website costs in 2026 depends on how complex the project is, but it usually ranges from a few hundred reais for simple landing pages to several thousand for custom web systems. The final price depends on factors like the number of pages, features, custom design and SEO optimization. Asking for a detailed quote is the most reliable way to know the real price for your case.

Before comparing prices, it's worth understanding what goes into this investment and why two sites that look alike can cost very different amounts. This guide explains the main price factors, the formats available and how to decide what makes sense for your business.

What determines the price of a professional website?

The price of a professional website depends on a set of technical and strategic variables, not just the number of pages. Understanding these factors helps you compare proposals fairly and avoid surprises halfway through the project.

  • Project complexity: a single-page landing page (LP) costs less than a company website with several sections or a system with a login area.
  • Custom design: a unique visual identity that matches the brand takes more hours of work than using ready-made templates.
  • Web development: custom-built sites with their own code tend to cost more than site builder solutions, but they deliver better performance and more flexibility.
  • SEO and GEO: optimizing the site to show up on Google and get cited by artificial intelligence (AI) assistants takes technical structure, well-written content and extra setup.
  • Integrations: connecting the site to payment systems, a CRM, WhatsApp or automation tools increases the scope and, with it, the price.
  • Maintenance and support: many projects include a post-launch support period or an ongoing maintenance plan, which also goes into the price.

How much does each type of website cost in 2026?

Each type of site serves a different goal, and the investment varies with that purpose. Here are the most common formats and what usually affects the price of each one.

Landing pages (LPs)

A landing page is a single page built for conversion, usually used in marketing campaigns or launches. Since the scope is leaner, it tends to be the most affordable professional website format, but the price goes up if it involves strategic copywriting, A/B testing or integration with automation tools.

Company websites

A company website presents the business, its services and contact channels, working as a digital business card. The cost varies with the number of pages, whether it needs a built-in blog and how much visual customization it has.

E-commerce and custom systems

Online stores and custom web systems, like a micro SaaS, involve more technical layers: a product catalog, payments, an admin dashboard and, in many cases, specific business rules. That's why they tend to be the biggest investments, with timelines and costs that vary a lot depending on how complex the features are.

Ready-made or custom site: which should you choose?

Choosing between a ready-made site and a custom one depends on the stage of the business and how much it relies on digital channels to sell. Templates and site builders cost less and deliver faster, but they have limits on customization and performance.

A custom-built site, on the other hand, grows with the business, allows specific integrations and usually performs better technically, which directly affects SEO. For businesses that depend on Google to generate leads, that technical care is usually worth the extra investment.

Why can cheaper sites end up costing more in the long run?

Very cheap sites usually rely on generic templates, limited hosting and little or no search engine optimization. That means that even if you save at launch, the business may spend more later fixing performance, security or Google ranking problems.

Some issues that often lead to rework when a site is built without technical planning:

  • No SEO structure, which makes it hard to show up in organic search.
  • No AI optimization (GEO), leaving the brand out of answers from assistants like ChatGPT, Gemini or Perplexity.
  • Non-responsive design, which hurts the experience on mobile.
  • No maintenance, which leaves the site exposed to bugs and outdated software.

How do you ask for a website quote without falling into traps?

Asking for a website quote takes clarity about what you expect from the project before you even talk to an agency or developer. That avoids unfair comparisons between proposals with different scopes.

  1. List the pages and features that are essential for launch.
  2. Decide whether the site needs a blog, a booking system or an online store.
  3. Ask whether the quote includes SEO, hosting and post-launch support.
  4. Confirm the estimated delivery date and the approval stages.
  5. Ask for examples of past projects in the same industry, when available.

Is a professional website worth it for local businesses?

For local businesses, like those in Santa Cruz do Rio Pardo/SP and the surrounding region, a professional website works as an extension of in-person service and of the Google Business Profile. It builds brand credibility, makes it easier to get in touch and helps the business show up for people searching for services in the city and nearby towns.

Businesses that serve all of Brazil remotely also benefit from a well-structured site, since it works as a storefront and a lead generation channel at any hour of the day.

How much a professional website costs: what to decide now

How much a professional website costs is a question that only has a precise answer once you define the type of project, the features you need and the level of SEO and GEO optimization you want. Instead of comparing only the final price between proposals, look at what each one includes: design, web development, support and search engine optimization.

Landing pages tend to be more affordable than company websites and custom systems.

faq.question: How much does a simple professional website cost?
faq.answer: A simple professional website, like a single-page landing page, is usually the most affordable website format. The exact price depends on how custom the design is and whether it needs features like forms or integrations with marketing tools.

faq.question: Is a ready-made site cheaper than a custom one?
faq.answer: Yes, ready-made sites or sites built with site builders usually have a lower upfront cost than custom web development projects. On the other hand, they offer less flexibility for customization and can limit the site's performance and SEO in the long run.

faq.question: What is included in a professional website quote?
faq.answer: A professional website quote usually includes design, development, hosting and, in many cases, a post-launch support period. Not every quote includes SEO or ongoing maintenance, so it's important to confirm those items before closing the deal.

faq.question: How long does it take to build a professional website?
faq.answer: The timeline for a professional website depends on how complex the project is. It can take just a few weeks for landing pages, or longer for custom systems with many features. It's best to confirm the schedule with the agency or developer before the project starts.

faq.question: Is it worth having a website even for a small or local business?
faq.answer: Yes, a professional website helps small and local businesses gain credibility and get found by people searching for their services on Google. For businesses in cities like Santa Cruz do Rio Pardo/SP, the site complements the Google Business Profile and extends their reach even beyond the area they serve in person.
